description: Somos un equipo de jóvenes apasionados por la ciencia, la tecnología y la exploración espacial. Nos interesan la programación, la robótica, la electrónica y la inteligencia artificial. Queremos participar en el NASA Space Apps Challenge para desarrollar ideas innovadoras, aprender nuevas habilidades y colaborar en el desafío 3. Buscamos integrantes creativos y responsables que tengan conocimientos.
summary:
I developed a 3D educational space simulator that runs directly in the browser with no installation required. In the game, players dock with the lunar Gateway from an Orion capsule, explore its modules, and resolve onboard emergencies. Afterward, they enter a mission center featuring four challenges:

Station Exploration: Players explore the spacecraft and complete Among Us-style minigames in each module.

Interplanetary Flight: Players launch, dodge meteoroids, and travel to Mars and Jupiter, collecting data upon landing.

Deep Space Investigation: Players investigate a lost team signal using clues based on NASA's Deep Space Network.

Unknown Planet Discovery: Players uncover the backstory of an uncharted planet.

Each completed mission adds 50% to a 0–200% progress bar. Once it reaches the maximum, the player travels to the Moon, experiences low-gravity walking, and plants a flag featuring their footprint and a custom quote.

This challenge is approached through active learning: every mission teaches real data about Orion, the Gateway, Mars, Jupiter, and the Deep Space Network. It is important because it brings space exploration closer to students in an interactive and motivating way, helping to inspire future scientific and technological vocations.
details:
Orion–Gateway Mission: 3D Educational Space Simulator

What It Is and How It Works

It is a browser-based simulator that requires no installation. The player experiences a complete journey: launching in an Orion capsule, docking with the lunar Gateway, exploring its modules, and resolving onboard emergencies. Afterward, they enter a mission center featuring four challenges, each teaching real NASA science through gameplay:

  1. Explore the Spacecraft. On-screen arrows point to each module: the Orion capsule, I-Hab, HALO, airlock, and PPE. Upon reaching each one, an Among Us-style minigame appears: aligning the docking mechanism, memorizing a code, connecting wires, pressurizing the airlock, and aligning solar panels.
  2. The Nearby Planet. A launch bar fills up as the engines fire. The player then dodges meteoroids on the way to Mars and Jupiter, collecting scientific data upon landing on Mars and Europa, Jupiter's moon.
  3. The Lost Signal. A fictional team stops transmitting. The player gathers four clues and must deduce what happened. The clues are based on real events and technology: the Deep Space Network, the 2018 dust storm that silenced the Opportunity rover, and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter acting as a communications relay.
  4. Unknown Planet. Four beacons tell the story of the fictional world Yachay-9b ("knowledge" in Quechua), inspired by NASA's research into ancient oceans, atmospheric loss, and biosignatures.

Each mission adds 50% to a 0–200% progress bar. Once completed, the player travels to the Moon, walks in lunar gravity (1/6 of Earth's), and plants a flag featuring their footprint and a custom quote.

Benefits

  • Turns facts usually read in a textbook into hands-on actions performed by the player.
  • Accessible: A single HTML file that runs on both computers and mobile phones.
  • Features visible progress and a personal reward, motivating players to complete the entire experience.

Expected Impact

We aim to bring space exploration closer to students who lack access to laboratories or specialized equipment, inspiring scientific and technological vocations. It can be used in the classroom as a wrap-up activity for a lesson on the Solar System or the Artemis program.

Tools

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
  • Three.js (WebGL) for 3D graphics.
  • 3D models of the Orion cabin and the Gateway, loaded in GLB format.
  • Procedurally generated textures, planets, terrain, and minigames.
  • An AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) used to code and refine the simulator.

Creativity

It combines spacecraft simulation, task-based minigames, and low-gravity exploration into a single experience. Furthermore, it blends real facts with fictional storytelling: the Ares-7 team and the planet Yachay-9b are invented, yet grounded in real NASA events. The final reward is personal: each player leaves their own custom quote and footprint on the Moon.

Factors We Considered

  • Rigor: Scientific data is based on real NASA missions and facts, while the stories of Ares-7 and Yachay-9b are fictional.
  • Accessibility: Requires no installation, account, or internet connection beyond the initial load.
  • Motivation: Short missions, immediate feedback, and a clear goal.
  • Current Limitations: The file is around 22 MB and may take some time to load on lower-end devices. Progress is not saved when the page is reloaded.
  • Next Steps: Implementing progress saving, adding more missions, and translating the simulator into other languages.
